decisions.reason: A same-message MODIFY already fully captures the required high-speed splash behavior and the permitted splash-control methods.
A same-message MODIFY already captures the requirement that mixing remain smooth and not become overly aggressive at higher speeds.
The client conditionally permits whisk-position adjustment as a splash-control measure but does not change the selected whisk head, material, size, or required position.
The source limits normal use at maximum speed but does not modify the independently stated reliability requirement for event use.
The source addresses mixing speed, frothing, and splash behavior, not beverage flow through the dispensing system.
Approval of a 3000 RPM motor does not itself change the confirmed 120V power source, battery policy, or power architecture.
The source does not specify a change to the base, feet, vibration resistance, or structural-stability design.
The motor-speed decision does not change the solenoid mechanism, button actuation, closed-state behavior, or dispensing isolation.
The client accepts the proposed 3000 RPM motor, necessarily changing the motor specification represented in the component-selection BOM.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
That makes sense — I like the idea of having more power and being able to control the speed range.

I think 3000 RPM works as long as we’re not running it at max all the time. Having the flexibility to dial it in for different mixing levels (slow mix vs higher-speed frothing) is actually ideal.

One thing I do want to make sure of with the higher RPM:
• we keep splashing under control
• the mixing stays smooth and doesn’t get too aggressive at higher speeds

So if needed, I’m open to adding a splash guard or dialing in whisk position / bowl depth to make sure it performs cleanly.

Overall I’m good with this direction.

decisions.reason: The client only conditionally permits bowl-depth adjustment if needed; no bowl capacity, form, size, or depth requirement is changed.
The source does not change any food-contact material selection or safety constraint.
The speed and splash-control decision does not change any bowl or spout cleaning requirement.
